No 20x result exists in the paper: tested ratios in LLMLingua-2's own tables top out at 14x (GSM8K half-shot, L2-032) with 5x on LongBench (L2-034); 15x is only stated as possible when combined with LLMLingua's budget controller, without a results table (L2-031). Losses are not minimal on every task: LongBench Synth. 21.3 vs 37.8 original (L2-034, L2-043), NaturalQuestions question-agnostic below zero-shot (L2-059, L2-061).

claim: Article says maintains 90%+ performance at moderate compression. The paper makes no such statement (no '90%' anywhere). Its tables mix cases above and below that level (e.g. MeetingBank QA near parity L2-040/L2-042; LongBench AVG 39.1 vs 44.0 at 5x L2-034/L2-043; BBH 61.94 vs 70.07 at 5x L2-033/L2-049; NaturalQuestions 39.9-48.6 vs 54.1-75.7 L2-059/L2-060). Ratios of these numbers are extractor arithmetic, not paper claims.
quote: 4. **Compression Quality**: Maintains 90%+ performance at moderate compression levels

claim: Article says it requires teacher models like GPT-4 for training. Supported only in the sense that the training labels were distilled from GPT-4-32k (L2-008, L2-083); the paper states the resulting dataset is publicly released (L2-101) and inference needs no GPT-4 call (L2-082). Training the released recipe from scratch on a new domain would need a teacher again.
quote: 1. **Data Distillation Dependency**: Requires access to high-quality teacher models (like GPT-4) for training

claim: Article lists compressing lengthy code prompts as a use case. On that column LLMLingua-2 scored 58.9 vs 54.2 original at 5x (L2-034, L2-043) while a no-context baseline scored 36.2 (L2-044).

claim: Article says Selective Context is currently limited to noun phrase boundaries. The 'noun-phrase-only' statement is a partial reading of a limitation, not a restriction on token/sentence modes.
quote: - Currently limited to noun phrase boundaries for syntactic preservation

claim: Article says Selective Context generally gets lower compression ratios than trained methods. The paper compares only against random deletion and the full context (no trained methods; SC-036 to SC-041) and treats the reduction ratio as a user-set parameter from 0.2 to 0.8 (SC-020); quality, not ratio, is what degrades at high reduction (SC-035, SC-050). In the LLMLingua-2 paper the SC baseline was run at the same ratios as other methods (SC-T01 to SC-T04), so the ratio is not inherently lower; its quality is lower there.
quote: 2. **Lower Compression Ratios**: Generally achieves lower compression than trained methods

claim: Article calls the method parameter-free, standalone and lightweight. The paper needs a base causal LM forward pass (LLaMA-7B or GPT-3 curie, SC-003/SC-004) plus spaCy and NLTK; in the LLMLingua-2 paper's run the SC baseline used a LLaMA-2-7B SLM, 26.5GB GPU memory and 15.5-15.9 s in the MeetingBank latency table on a V100-32G (SC-T08, SC-T07, SC-T09). It is training-free, not model-free.
